criteria.criterion: defaults.toml gains three [[default]] entries with unique ids (outcome-check, no-empty-success, thrash-stop), each applies_to ["*"] (or classes that include docs), each with a source citing this request, and each statement's first sentence states the core rule, since render shows only that sentence.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: defaults.toml gains three entries with these ids. Each has applies_to = ["*"] and a source that cites job 20261015-095214-1egb. Each first sentence states the core rule, and the new test checks the rendered first-sentence lines. The existing duplicate check (repository_defaults_parse) still passes, so the ids are unique.

criteria.criterion: The outcome-check statement says: the outcome is the check behind the work, not the activity; for audience-facing quality a fresh model reader that took no part in the work rates the live result as a newcomer, and a rating below 4 of 5 blocks completion. no-empty-success says an empty queue or finished list never counts as success alone. thrash-stop says that if the same item fails twice in a loop, the loop stops and reports thrashing.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: all three statements use the request's own wording almost word for word. Each also adds a sentence marking it prose-only, as the reading assumed.

criteria.criterion: The reader prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md) tells the reader to record applicable standing defaults of this kind as acceptance criteria and not to ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff, reader.md adds: "Standing defaults like outcome-check apply unasked: record each applicable one as an acceptance criterion; do not ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise."

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: a new test loads the repository defaults.toml, selects defaults for class docs (an explainer page request), and shows the three defaults appear in the rendered default list; the existing parse, duplicate and render tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: 65 passed, including defaults::tests::an_explainer_page_request_gets_the_three_standing_defaults, repository_defaults_parse, duplicates_are_refused and render_shows_only_the_first_sentence. The new test keeps only defaults that apply to '*' or docs, checks the three rendered lines, and checks that the code-only `rust` default is left out, so the selection is real.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` for the workspace: a new test builds the reader brief for the request 'write an explainer page' and shows it contains the three defaults and the instruction to turn them into acceptance criteria, with no question field required; a rival check shows a request that says otherwise is not forced to carry them if the reader prompt supports that wording.
criteria.evidence: Every suite passed, with no failures. The new test briefs::tests::an_explainer_page_request_gets_the_standing_defaults_without_a_question builds the reader brief for 'write an explainer page' and checks that it has no 'Question asked'. It then assembles the reader's system prompt in the same order as athena-core/src/reading.rs (contract, reader prompt, rendered defaults) and checks that it contains the three defaults, the instruction to record them as acceptance criteria, and the 'unless the request says otherwise' wording. That rival check only tests the wording, which is what the criterion allows.
Both printed nothing, which means clean. Athena's own run with -D warnings also passed.

summary: I'm passing this change. It adds three standing defaults to defaults.toml: outcome-check, no-empty-success and thrash-stop. Each applies to every class of request, and each says it is prose-only (no loop code enforces it yet). The reader prompt now tells the reader to record each applicable standing default as an acceptance criterion without asking, unless the request says otherwise. To make room for that line, the prompt was shortened, because the reader prompt has a fixed size budget. Two new tests show that a request to write an explainer page gets all three defaults with no question to the user. The second test builds the reader's prompt the same way the real code in athena-core/src/reading.rs does. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data` (65 passed), `cargo test` for the whole workspace (all passed), and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` (both clean). Three small problems, none blocking: the design doc now says defaults.toml has 15 entries, but I counted 16; the shortened prompt dropped the line "Read the files the request touches."; and one edited paragraph in the design doc is not wrapped like the lines around it. All results are from the snapshot; none depend on records/.
